author: graham
subject: Purchase of 9 Quillon Gardens: contract pack and exchange arrangements

messages.text:
Dear Ms Okafor,

Further to our conversation of Friday last, I write to enclose the contract pack for your purchase of 9 Quillon Gardens, Wexcombe, at the agreed price of £425,000, together with the seller's replies to our preliminary enquiries and the official copy of the register. I have read all of these with some care and, subject to the points below, I see no reason why we should not proceed towards exchange.

So that we may keep to the timetable that you have indicated, there are three matters on which I require your attention:

(a) Contract and Transfer. Please sign the enclosed contract in the places marked in pencil, and have your signature witnessed by an adult who is not a party to the transaction and who does not live with you. The signed contract should reach this office, in original, by 12 noon on Friday 20 November 2026. A scan will not do for this purpose, although you may send one in advance so that I can check it. Please do not date the document; that will be done on exchange.

(b) Deposit. The contract provides for a deposit of ten per cent of the price, namely £42,500. We shall need that sum in cleared funds in our client account no later than Wednesday 25 November 2026, so that we are in a position to exchange on or about Friday 27 November 2026. The sum should be sent only to the account details on the enclosed letter, and I should add (without wishing to alarm you) that you should verify those details by telephone to me before sending anything. I have received your earlier transfer of £1,150 in respect of searches and have credited it to your matter; it forms no part of the deposit.

(c) Insurance. I note that you have not yet told me that you have arranged buildings insurance. Under the contract the risk passes to you on exchange and not on completion, and the policy must therefore be in force from the day of exchange. Please let me have a copy of the policy schedule, showing the sum insured and the start date, before we exchange. If you wish me to chase your lender about their insurance requirements, say so and I shall do it, but the policy itself is yours to arrange.

For the avoidance of doubt, the completion date proposed in the draft contract, Friday 11 December 2026, is provisional and remains subject to the seller's own purchase. I shall confirm it when we exchange and not before. Nothing in this letter should be read as a commitment by either party to a particular date.

I am in the office every day this week except Thursday afternoon, and I shall be glad to go through the documents with you at any time.

Yours sincerely,

Graham Pemberton-Hale
Partner | Pemberton-Hale & Aske LLP
Fourteen Lantern Row, Wexcombe
T: 01000 555 0142 | graham@pemberton-hale.example

author: graham
subject: Practice Note 14/26: changes to the property transaction forms

messages.text:
Dear Member,

The Property Section has published a revised set of standard enquiry forms with effect from 1 February 2027. The principal changes are a shorter fixtures and fittings list, a new question on flood history, and an amended question on building safety. Members using the previous forms may continue to do so for contracts exchanged before the effective date. A seminar on the changes will be held on 9 December 2026; places are limited and booking is optional.

This note is for information only and does not constitute legal advice. No action is required.

--
The Wexcombe Law Society is a body established for the benefit of members. This email is confidential. Unsubscribe from notices at any time via the link in your member profile. Views expressed are those of the author and not necessarily of the Society.

mustNotClaim: The seminar is not mandatory

author: graham
subject: Sale and purchase, 14 Oldfield Road: completion date and enquiries

messages.text:
Dear Ms Quill,

I act for the buyers of 14 Oldfield Road at £485,000. Further to your draft contract, I raise three enquiries: (1) the Japanese knotweed report; (2) planning permission for the loft conversion; (3) the boundary on the eastern side. I should be glad of replies by 28 October, and propose completion on 11 December 2026.

Yours sincerely,
Graham

Dear Mr P-H, sorry for the delay. (1) The report is attached, no knotweed. (2) Building regs certificate attached; planning is under review with the council. (3) The boundary is the fence shown on the plan. Completion 11 Dec fine from our side.

Dear Ms Quill,

Thank you. On (2), "under review" will not do: I need the planning permission or a written statement that none was required, and I cannot recommend exchange without it. On (3), please confirm who owns the fence. Also, the lender's valuation was £478,000, so the mortgage offer is £430,000 and the buyers' equity needs £55,000, which they are arranging.

Yours sincerely,
Graham
Mr P-H, planning: the council has indicated a response by 20 November. Our onward purchase has hit a snag; can we move completion to Friday 18 December? Fence is the seller's.

Dear Ms Quill,

18 December is acceptable to my clients provided exchange is by 4 December. 11 December falls away. I shall expect the planning evidence by 25 November, so that I have time to advise before 4 December. I have noted your answer that the fence belongs to the seller and shall report to my clients.

Yours sincerely,
Graham

othersOwe: Quill to supply planning permission, or a written statement that none was required, by 25 November 2026
Buyers to arrange £55,000 equity (their side)
settled: Completion date is moved to 18 December 2026 (conditional on exchange by 4 December)
Seller owns the eastern fence
No knotweed per the report
mustNotClaim: Completion on 11 December has been dropped
The planning point is not resolved

author: graham
subject: Estate of Mrs E. Larkin: sale of 3 Mill Cottages and distribution

messages.text: Dear Mr Larkin, as co-executor you must sign the contract to sell 3 Mill Cottages at £268,000 by 9 October. I enclose it. Graham
Graham, signed and witnessed, posted today. My sister wants the Dresden clock out of the house before completion. Who decides? J
Dear Mr Larkin, the will leaves the contents equally to you and your sister. Neither may remove an item unless both agree in writing. I suggest you sign an agreed schedule. Graham
Mr Pemberton-Hale, I haven't agreed to anything. The clock was promised to me by Mum. Please do not let Julian take it. Pippa

Dear Ms Larkin, I cannot take sides. The clock stays in the house, and I will see that the locks are changed on the day of exchange. Please send me by 23 October your wishes in writing on the contents. Graham
Dear colleagues, exchange of contracts on 3 Mill Cottages took place today at £268,000. Completion is on 20 November 2026. Deposit of £26,800 held.
Written wishes attached, sorry for the delay. I would take the clock and the piano, Julian the desk and the clocks in the hall, the rest sold at auction.
Fine on the clock if she drops the piano. Otherwise I won't sign.

Dear Mr and Ms Larkin,

Completion is 20 November. Before then I need, from each of you, a signed contents schedule or a written statement that you disagree. If you disagree I shall put the contents to the auctioneer for the sale and hold the proceeds. I shall also distribute the net sale proceeds, after costs and the funeral account of £4,950, equally. The deadline for the schedule is Friday 13 November.

Yours sincerely,
Graham

othersOwe: Julian and Pippa Larkin to sign a contents schedule or state disagreement by 13 November 2026
Graham to distribute proceeds after completion
settled: Contracts were exchanged on 26 October at £268,000 with a £26,800 deposit
Completion is 20 November 2026
mustNotClaim: The contents are not agreed: the clock and piano are disputed
Julian's 'fine on the clock' is conditional, not agreement

author: graham
subject: Invoice currency: Wójcik & Sons / Bellmoor

messages.text:
Dear Ms Wójcik,

Further to our call, the contract sum is €48,000 payable in euros under clause 5. Bellmoor's finance director has asked that it instead be invoiced in sterling at £41,400. Please advise (1) whether you are willing to invoice in sterling at all; (2) if so, at what rate; (3) whether you require payment of the first tranche of €12,000 by 20 November as the contract says. I make no recommendation until I have your answers.

Yours sincerely,
Graham
Mr Pemberton-Hale, I would accept sterling only at the rate on the invoice date plus 1.5%. I need the €12,000 first tranche by 20 Nov. I cannot say more before talking to my brother.

Bellmoor to pay the first tranche of €12,000 by 20 November

subject: Water damage claim: kitchen and hallway

messages.text: Hi Graham, a pipe burst in the kitchen on Saturday. Floor and hall carpet ruined. Who do I tell?
Dear Ms Voss, notify your insurer at once and take dated photographs. I recommend that you do not throw anything away until the adjuster has seen it. Graham
Reported. Claim number HM-90417. Adjuster is called Piers.
Hello Eleanor, visited today. Estimate for repairs £6,940 inc. VAT; excess £500. Need two builder quotes by 30 Oct.
Piers, one quote only so far: £7,300. The second builder is away until next week.
OK, new date for the second quote is 13 November. No further extension.
Graham, got the second quote: £6,750. Sending to Piers today. Should I start the work?
Dear Ms Voss, do not start until Piers has approved in writing, otherwise the insurer may decline to pay. Graham
Got both quotes. We'll go with £6,750 less £500 excess, so £6,250 to be paid. I'll send an authorisation Monday, then work can start.
Great, thanks both. I'll wait for Monday's email.
